question: PulseCommerce has a ProductMarkdownSpecification component that imports a 180 KB Markdown and syntax-highlighting library and requires zero browser interactivity. Which boundary should it use?
options: A Client Component ('use client') wrapped in useMemo so the browser caches the parsed HTML
A Server Component (no directive) so the 180 KB library executes on the server and adds 0 KB to the client JavaScript bundle
A Server Action ('use server') invoked inside useEffect after hydration
A next/form <Form> component with a POST action
explanation: Server Components run exclusively on the server. Keeping ProductMarkdownSpecification as a Server Component ensures the 180 KB library is never downloaded, parsed, or executed by the browser.

question: SupplierWholesaleMarginCalculator reads confidential supplier wholesale contracts to compute public retail price tiers and has no browser state. Why must it be a Server Component?
options: Because browser JavaScript cannot perform floating-point multiplication accurately
Because executing wholesale contract logic in a Server Component (guarded by server-only) ensures confidential supplier rates never enter the client bundle or serialized RSC payload
Because Client Components cannot render numbers inside HTML tables
Because Next.js automatically encrypts all Client Component props with the user's password
explanation: Running confidential pricing logic inside a Server Component keeps wholesale contract data and secrets strictly on the server, sending only the computed public retail price tiers to the browser.

question: Why should CatalogFilterSearchForm (which navigates to /search?q=... with URL query parameters) use <Form> from next/form instead of a 'use server' Server Action?
options: Because Server Actions cannot read strings longer than 10 characters
Because <Form action="/search"> serializes inputs into shareable URL search parameters, prefetches the /search layout and loading state, and performs a soft GET navigation
Because next/form automatically indexes the user's local filesystem
Because Server Actions only work in production builds and fail in development
explanation: Search and filter forms represent idempotent GET navigations that belong in the URL query string. <Form action="/search"> from next/form provides layout prefetching and soft client navigation with URL search parameters.

question: In an Architecture Decision Record (ADR), why is documenting negative consequences just as important as documenting positive consequences?
options: It satisfies linter rules that count the number of bullet points in a file
It makes the engineering trade-offs explicit—such as React Flight prop serialization rules and strict server/client import boundaries—so the team anticipates and designs around them
It prevents Next.js from compiling the application if any trade-off is omitted
It automatically generates unit tests from negative bullet points
explanation: Every architectural choice involves trade-offs. Recording negative consequences (like prop serialization constraints across 'use client' boundaries) helps engineers understand the operational rules of the chosen architecture.
